summary: Tested repair quote serial management end-to-end (backend + UI). Backend: 9/9 pytest pass (reception -> Recibido, create repair quote -> Cotizado, PUT sync multiline N:N release/keep, add Recibido serial, duplicate new_version transfer + PUT unmark, in_place + PUT sync, non-repair PUT untouched, reception PDF embeds logo image). Frontend: found and FIXED a CRITICAL bug — GET /api/quotes (response_model=List[Quote]) stripped equipment_items[].serials/no_serial and repair_models, so EditEquipRepairDialog showed 0/qty for every line and the pool lacked the quote's own serials ('En esta cotización' missing). After fix, UI flow fully verified: counters 2/2,1/1; origin badges correct; qty increase without serials -> error toast & justification blocked; adjusting serials + justification saves; DB confirms new version owns S1,S2,S3 (Cotizado) and original has linked=[] + released ids; in_place mode unmarking S3 returns it to Recibido.

critical.issue: FIXED by testing agent: Pydantic response models dropped repair serial data. EquipmentQuoteItem (models.py) lacked serials/no_serial and Quote lacked repair_models/linked_taller_equipo_ids. Consequence before fix: edit dialog lost all serials; if client had no 'Recibido' equipment, validation was skipped and the PUT sent serials:[] -> sync_repair_serials would RELEASE all serials of the quote (silent data loss).

minor.issue: Original quote keeps stale equipment_items[].serials and repair_models after its serials are transferred; if original is edited/approved later its PDF/dialog still shows serials owned by the new version (sync won't steal them, but display is misleading).

ui_bugs.issue: Success toast always says 'Nueva versión X (vN) creada exitosamente' even in mode=in_place; footer text 'La cotización original v1 permanece intacta' is inaccurate for repair new_version (its serials are released) and for in_place.

action_items: Review/keep testing-agent fix in backend/models.py (EquipmentQuoteItem.serials/no_serial, Quote.repair_models/linked_taller_equipo_ids as Optional with [] defaults). Check other endpoints using response_model=Quote/EquipmentQuoteItem return the same fields.
Defensive: in EditEquipRepairDialog, block save for repair quotes when a line has quantity>0 and 0 serials even if pool is empty, or fetch full quote via GET /quotes/{id} before opening the dialog.
Adjust toast/footer copy per editMode (in_place vs new_version).
Optional: on new_version transfer, clear or mark serials in the original quote's equipment_items/repair_models.
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend flow duplicates first then PUTs; if PUT fails after new_version the serials already moved to an orphan Borrador quote (no rollback).
transfer_repair_serials sets 'En reparación' serials back to 'Cotizado' in new version — acceptable but confirm business intent.
Test runs consume quote number sequence (COT-2026-11-00x) even though fixtures are deleted.

success_rate.frontend: 100% after backend model fix (was failing before)

seed_data_creation: All fixtures cleaned up: TEST_ clients, TST- taller_equipos, test quotes, related bitacora/client_logs. Verified 0 remaining.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login UI via API: POST /api/auth/login then localStorage.setItem('session_token'), goto /dashboard then /quotes. ui_fixture_repair_serials.py setup|teardown SUF creates client + 3 received serials + repair quote. Modify flow: quote-actions-{id} -> modify-quote-btn-{id} -> modify-choice-new-version|in-place.
rca of the issue: Root cause: GET /api/quotes uses response_model=List[Quote]; Pydantic filtered unknown fields so serials per line and repair_models never reached the frontend although stored in Mongo. Repro: create repair quote with serials, open Modificar -> counters 0/qty. Mitigation applied: added fields to models.py.
